proposal_after_tax.assumptions: Illustrative liquidation at scheduled values, not tax due on divorce or a guaranteed judicial equalization amount. Wife sells the $1,100,000 house alone, pays 6% ($66,000) selling costs, qualifies for a $250,000 section 121 exclusion, and pays 15% capital-gains tax plus 3.8% NIIT on $484,000 taxable gain: ($1,100,000-$66,000-$300,000-$250,000)*18.8%=$90,992. House after-tax equity=$1,100,000-$66,000-$400,000-$90,992=$543,008; plus $50,000 cash and $20,000 car=$613,008. Husband's $400,000 pretax 401(k) is valued at $304,000 after assumed 24% future withdrawal tax; brokerage is $288,000 after 15% of its $80,000 gain; plus $50,000 cash and $20,000 car=$662,000. This mixes a possible future house sale with hypothetical future retirement withdrawals, so the amounts are bargaining illustrations, not present cash or a forecast. Assumes all brokerage gain is long-term, no brokerage NIIT, unchanged values/basis, no other taxes or sale costs. Brokerage NIIT treatment is not specified by the closed library; if an additional 3.8% applied to its $80,000 gain, Husband's modeled value would fall by $3,040 to $658,960 and the gap to $45,952. Without the assumed house NIIT, Wife's value would rise to $631,400 and the gap would fall to $30,600. Residence eligibility, future sale price, actual tax rates and brokerage lots are unverified. Authorities: library/irc_1041_121_71.md; library/tax_rates_assumed.md.

maintenance_tax_treatment: For a post-2018 divorce instrument, $2,000 per month for 36 months is neither deductible by Husband nor taxable to Wife; strike the contrary proposal language. Total nominal maintenance is $72,000. It remains an income adjustment on the Columbia child-support worksheet. Authority: library/irc_1041_121_71.md; library/columbia_child_support_guidelines.md.
dependents_and_filing_status: Filing status depends on marital status on December 31. If the decree is final by then, each files single unless eligible for head of household; Wife may qualify for head of household if the children live with her more than half the year and she pays more than half the cost of the home. With approximately 70% of overnights, Wife is the custodial parent for the dependency rule. Husband may take a child tax credit in an alternating year only if Wife signs Form 8332 for that child/year; that release does not transfer head-of-household status, EITC, or dependent-care credit. The decree date, household-cost payer, and any Form 8332 agreement remain unknown. Authority: library/filing_status_dependents.md.
